name: GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc.
moat_justification: A differentiated specialty foundry, not a scale leader: GF exited the leading-edge race and leads in specialty platforms (RF SOI, silicon germanium, silicon photonics/Fotonix, FD-SOI, BCD power) designed into long-life automotive, industrial, IoT and communications programs, where re-qualification makes switching slow and expensive, and its US/EU/Singapore footprint is a scarce secure-supply asset that governments fund (CHIPS awards and LOIs). Against that: roughly 3% pure-play foundry revenue share against TSMC's ~73% (Q2 2026), share slipping from 4%, no leading-edge offering, mature-node price competition from UMC/SMIC and Chinese capacity, and returns that have not held through a cycle (net losses in 2019-20, a $935M Malta impairment driving the 2024 net loss, owner's earnings negative in the 2022 capex peak). Net: moderate/narrow moat, 5/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, cover page, securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b): 'Ordinary shares, par value US$0.02 per share', trading symbol GFS, Nasdaq Global Select Market; the company's prospectus supplement dated March 11, 2026 (Form 424B7, filer's own filing) likewise states the ordinary shares 'are listed and traded on Nasdaq under the symbol "GFS"' and quotes prices per ordinary share — the Nasdaq security is the ordinary share itself, not an ADS) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Capex-heavy specialty foundry, moat 5/10 — at $48.94 the weighted IRR is only 6.0% (weighted IV@15% $13.23), so it does not clear the 15% hurdle; it would need a price at or below ~$13.23 to clear 15% on these numbers.
moat_for: Specialty platform leadership (RF SOI, SiGe, silicon photonics/Fotonix, FD-SOI, power BCD) in nodes the leading-edge players largely vacated
High switching costs: designs are qualified into long-life automotive/industrial/IoT programs and are slow and costly to re-qualify at another fab

Scarce geographically diversified secure supply (Malta NY, Dresden, Singapore, Vermont) backed by US/EU government funding — CHIPS awards/LOIs including $375M quantum and a $300M silicon-photonics LOI in 2026
AI data-center optical demand inflecting: communications infrastructure & data center revenue +62% YoY in Q2 2026, guided +50-60% for FY2026, silicon photonics revenue expected to more than double
moat_against: Subscale: ~3% pure-play foundry revenue share vs TSMC ~73% in Q2 2026, and GF's share slipped from 4% in 2025 — no scale or cost leadership
No leading-edge nodes: the industry's fastest-growing, highest-margin wafer demand is structurally out of reach
Mature-node price competition from UMC, SMIC and expanding Chinese capacity caps pricing power in its core nodes
Capex intensity eats the cash flow: owner's earnings were negative in 2022 (capex $3,059M) and swing with the fab investment cycle; returns on capital run mid-single digits
Cyclical end markets: automotive and smart-mobile weakness offset data-center strength in the 2026 prints, and the 2023-24 downturn cut revenue from $8,108M to $6,750M
